evidence: Rotating momentum-exchange skyhooks with carbon nanotube tethers appear only in concept studies and papers; none has been built or flown.
Carpinteri & Pugno (2008) and an MIT thesis model nanotube-cable super-bridges with spans of 5+ km, but no nanotube bridge cable has been built.

Multilayer graphene grown in situ on X70 pipeline steel cut hydrogen diffusion about 123-fold, and slow-strain-rate tests showed resistance to embrittlement (lab demonstration); UK National Gas is also testing graphene internal barriers.
Curved Ag/Al2O3 multilayer hyperlenses (cylindrical in 2007, spherical later) have imaged sub-diffraction objects (125-205 nm) in the far field; live-virus imaging has not been shown.

Water-wave cloaks made of arrays of bottom-mounted pillars or shaped bathymetry steer waves around a protected region in lab tanks (Liverpool/CNRS 2008; Zhejiang 60 m wave-tank harbour tests); none has been installed in the field.

A UCSF pilot trial (NCT07866768) is testing a wearable focused-ultrasound device for glymphatic clearance, and wearable glymphatic monitors exist, but no closed-loop sleep-triggered system with a skull-correcting lens has been demonstrated.
No isotope-patterned (12C/13C) diamond storage read by Raman shift was found; diamond storage work uses NV/ND1 defects, and 13C Raman barcodes have been shown only in polymers.

Self-healing perovskite encapsulants have been demonstrated only with intrinsic polymers (ion-aggregate epoxy, Science Advances 2025); no microcapsule-based crack-sealing encapsulant for perovskite modules was found.

Carbon nanotube yarn and tape tethers for electrodynamic-tether deorbit kits are in development and were planned for CubeSats, but no confirmed in-orbit deorbit with a nanotube tether was found (TEPCE used a non-CNT tether).
Sorbent-bed extraction of water from Martian air (WAVAR with zeolite, MOFs pitched for Mars) exists only as concepts and technical reports; there is no Mars-condition demonstration.
MOFs (UiO-66, MOF-808/GO) are studied as urea and uremic-toxin sorbents for wearable-kidney dialysate regeneration, but no wearable unit with MOF ammonia adsorption was found.

Dang et al. (Green Energy & Environment 2024) demonstrated a CO2-capture temperature swing driven by passive radiative cooling and solar heating, using activated carbon rather than a MOF; a SUNY-Buffalo DOE project did the same for DAC with membrane sorbents.

A passive subambient daytime radiative cooling coating on a grain silo kept the wheat pile about 10 C cooler than an uncoated control (Heliyon 2023), and a radiative-cooling metafilm was field-tested on a real granary (Building and Environment 2024).
No overhead radiative-cooling shade net that passes photosynthetic light was found; the closest work is radiative-cooling soil mulch films field-tested to reduce plant heat stress.

Reviews list MOFs among emerging oxygen sources for thick engineered tissue, but demonstrated oxygen-releasing scaffolds use calcium peroxide or perfluorocarbons; no MOF oxygen-loaded scaffold was found.

Graphene-oxide membranes have been studied as proton-permselective membranes for recovering acid from metal-laden waste (J. Membrane Sci. 2021), but no demonstration on battery-recycling leachate with pristine graphene proton transport was found.
Electrocaloric cooling prototypes exist at lab scale (e.g. 20.9 C span, 4.2 W, Science), and solar vaccine fridges use compressors or thermoelectrics, but no electrocaloric vaccine fridge was found.
Topological-insulator surface states have been studied for boosting thermoelectric zT, and wearable Bi2Te3 generators exist, but no wearable that exploits TI surface states was found.

Superhydrophobic air-trapping surfaces resisted thrombosis in rabbit carotid tube implants and in ex vivo blood tests, and patents describe superhydrophobic stents, but no air-layer stent has been demonstrated in vivo.
Colloidal quantum dots in neuronal membranes detected depolarization optically in cultured cells (Nano Letters 2019), but no in vivo brain-interface use has been shown.

The University of Exeter iGEM PETexe project built a washing-machine outlet filter that traps microfibres and digests them with PETase/MHETase into terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol, reportedly about 75% of fibres.

A lab test showed a light sail made of opposing diffraction gratings being pushed by a laser beam and re-centring itself in it (Swartzlander, PRL 2019); metasurface versions so far exist only in simulation, and nothing has flown.

SINTEF has studied epoxy insulation with monomer-filled microcapsules that burst and fill electrical trees, for subsea connectors and offshore grids, but only at material or lab scale and not in a cable.

Manchester (Nature Communications 2017) electrochemically pumped protons through graphene membranes, separating hydrogen from deuterium with a factor of about 8 and projecting plant-scale output; this is a lab demonstration with no pilot plant.

3D-printed binary acoustic metasurfaces corrected skull aberration to focus ultrasound through ex vivo human skulls (Frontiers in Neuroscience 2022), but none has been used for transcranial functional ultrasound imaging.
